reasons: The main tab body was not shown, so its error handling cannot be judged.
Server data is not checked at run time.

terms.meaning: Word for word, as the source wrote it.
A reference to a source that includes the quote and where it came from.
One execution of a tool over a set of projects.
A written record of every decision made.
Kept back from use, with a stated reason.

sections.name: File setup
sections.title: Imports
sections.what: Brings in React, the data fetching tool, the link helper, the server call helper and the citation helper.

sections.name: RunRecord, RunMeta, Payload
sections.title: Shapes of run records
sections.what: Describes one record from a run, which may be a value used, a calculation, a research fact or a reason signal. Each has its source, quote, date and any conflict with other values. Also describes each run and the full response for a project.
sections.why: Gives the screen a fixed shape for the data it displays.
sections.watch_out: The screen relies on the server sending this shape. A missing field may show as blank rather than as an error.

sections.name: FIELD_LABEL, fieldLabel, ORIGIN_LABEL, KIND_LABEL, TOOL_LABEL, runHref, norm
sections.title: Plain labels and helpers
sections.what: Turns internal field names such as planned capex into readable labels, names where values came from and which tool produced them, builds the link for each run, and cleans text for comparison.
sections.why: So the owner reads Planned budget rather than internal codes.
sections.watch_out: Any tool name not in the list sends its link to the Reality Scan page by default, which may be the wrong place.

sections.name: dateOf
sections.title: Date formatting
sections.what: Shows a date in short form, such as 5 Mar 2025, or the word undated when the date is missing.
sections.why: Keeps dates readable for the owner.
sections.watch_out: Dates follow the viewer's local format, so the same date can look different on another computer.

sections.name: OpenCitation
sections.title: Citation opener type and context
sections.what: Defines the shape of a function that opens the full citation for a record, and a shared context that lets the citation display reach it.
sections.why: Likely reason: lets a deeply nested part open the citation popup without passing the function down every level.
sections.watch_out: If no parent provides the opener, citations still show their quotes but lose their open buttons.

sections.name: Citation
sections.title: Citation display
sections.what: Shows the verbatim quote, a link to the source, the publisher and date, a button to show the full passage, and any review notes on the record.
sections.why: Lets the owner check each figure against its source in place.
sections.watch_out: Quotes are shown as stored. The component does not check them against the source.

sections.name: ValueCell
sections.title: Value display
sections.what: Shows the value, with a tilde if it is approximate, plus currency and unit. It also shows the hold reason and any source check that disagrees with the value.
sections.why: Keeps conflicts beside the value so they are not missed.
sections.watch_out: A conflict is hidden when its text matches the hold reason, so a repeated message is not shown twice.

sections.name: RunLinks
sections.title: Run links
sections.what: Lists the three most recent runs that included this project as links to their pages, with a button to show more when there are more than three.
sections.why: Keeps the list short while leaving every run reachable.
sections.watch_out: Runs without a completion date sort unpredictably, because a missing date cannot be compared.

sections.name: RunRecordsTab (part 1)
sections.title: Loading and grouping run records
sections.what: When the Run records tab opens, it fetches every record kept for the project. It shows a short message while loading, on error, or when no run has included the project yet. It then groups the records by field and works out which fields hold more than one different value.
sections.why: The code comment says identical values from different runs are collapsed, and each different value keeps its own citation. Lesson passages are left out of the count of differing values, which the comment says is intentional.
sections.watch_out: Duplicates are matched on the value, the link, the statement and the origin together, so changing any one of those changes which entries count as the same.

sections.name: RunRecordsTab (part 2)
sections.title: Summary numbers, filters and records table
sections.what: At the top are a run picker, four summary numbers (fields recorded, fields with several values, sources admitted, calculations) and a checkbox that limits the table to conflicting fields. Below is a table showing each field's values with origin, check status, verbatim citation and the runs that used it. A red badge marks fields with more than one distinct value.
sections.why: The page says these records sit alongside the project and do not change its own fields, and that every disagreeing value is kept with its own citation. The table shows disagreements openly rather than hiding them.
sections.watch_out: The summary numbers count raw records, while the table merges duplicates, so the numbers will not match the number of table rows.

sections.name: RunRecordsTab (part 3)
sections.title: Panel of research items held back
sections.what: A button shows or hides a list of research items that were refused at collection, not found, or held by review. Each row gives the field, the reason, the citation or value, and the date of the run.
sections.why: Likely reason: gaps and rejections stay visible to the owner without being mixed into the main table of values.
sections.watch_out: The list follows the run picker above, so a held item from another run stays hidden until that run or All runs is chosen.

summary: For one project, shows every value and calculation used in each tool run, with its verbatim source quote, source link and any conflicts between sources.
purpose: Gives the owner a traceable record of where each figure about a project came from.
why: The header says the list is read only and does not change the project's own fields. Likely reason: to make every number checkable.
how: 1. Load all run records for the project. 2. Show each run as a date link, most recent first, with three shown at first. 3. For each record, show its label, its value with any hold reason or conflict, and its citation with quote, source and date. 4. Offer buttons to open the full citation and to show the full passage. The main tab body, which groups the records, is not shown in this packet, so its exact steps are unclear.
inputs: The project id and the server response listing runs and records. A citation opener is supplied by a parent component.
outputs: A read-only display of records, quotes, links and buttons. Nothing is saved.
risks: The screen shows raw server data without checking it. Runs without dates sort unpredictably. Unknown tool names send links to the Reality Scan page. Citations lose their open buttons if no citation opener is supplied.
debug: If a value is missing, find the record in the run ledger on the server and check its field name. If a link opens the wrong tool, check the tool name. If citations have no button, check that a citation opener is provided. If runs are out of order, check that they have completion dates.
